tagline: Two days, two trails, pines one way and Gulf the other.
intro: Out of Tallahassee the city lights give way to two trails, one through tall pines and one along the Gulf. The Gulf road follows US 98 from Newport through Medart, Panacea and Carrabelle to Apalachicola, with spurs down to St. Marks and out to St. George Island. Its keepers recommend two days at the least.

This is where the Gulf Coast curves westward, a shore of seagrass beds, marshes and winding rivers. More than 300 kinds of birds live in the region, and about 30 species of carnivorous plants, more than in any area its size in the world.

moments.title: St. Marks Light
moments.text: Florida's second-oldest light station stands at the mouth of the St. Marks River on Apalachee Bay. The first tower built for it was turned down for having hollow walls.

moments.title: Sopchoppy
moments.text: The 1894 depot, now a museum, served a line locals called the Gopher, Frog and Alligator, which hauled turpentine, honey, oysters in iced barrels and caviar from Sopchoppy River sturgeon.

moments.title: Carrabelle
moments.text: A Gulf town at the mouth of the Carrabelle River, named for its founder's niece, who became its first postmaster. The hurricane of 1899 left it nine homes.
